touches.text: Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal.
The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict.

The verdict's instrument run is a seal-grade run, so it runs where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), under bubblewrap. A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's. - CC

conflicts.ticket_says: validate door refuses a criterion whose instrument does not extract to a command the sealer can start; for repo paths, extract_command returns None when git index mode is 100644 (not executable), so validate refuses them and nothing berths
conflicts.why: Outline 9.4.8.1 describes a box without required tools (Windows) accepting instruments and deferring their execution to the sealer at verdict time: 'A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's.' The ticket refuses such instruments at validate time (refusing any repo path with index 100644), preventing Windows from drafting them entirely. This contradicts the outline's model where Windows can draft instruments it cannot run directly, leaving the actual run to the sealer. A Python test script correctly has index mode 100644 (not directly executable) because it runs via python, not directly—but the ticket refuses it anyway, breaking valid instruments that specify their execution method.
